data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical immunomodulators & antipsoriatics_

**Class:** Synthetic anthrone (derived from chrysarobin of Goa powder)

## Mechanism of action
- Generates free radicals (oxidation) → inhibits keratinocyte proliferation and mitochondrial function; also reduces neutrophil and T-cell activity

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic plaque psoriasis (thick, stable plaques; especially in children or when steroids should be avoided) — inpatient Ingram regimen (with tar baths and UVB) or outpatient short-contact therapy
- Alopecia areata (irritant therapy — off-label)

## Dose & formulations
- Short-contact therapy: start 0.1–0.5% for 10–30 min daily, increase to 1–3% as tolerated, then wash off
- Ingram regimen: tar bath → UVB → dithranol in Lassar's paste (with salicylic acid to stabilise) overnight
- Apply to plaques only; protect surrounding skin with petroleum jelly

## Adverse effects
- Irritation and burning of surrounding normal skin ('dithranol burn')
- Purple-brown staining of skin, nails, hair, clothes, bathtubs (oxidation products) — skin staining fades in 1–2 weeks
- Perilesional pigmentation as a sign of clearing

## Contraindications
- Acute, erythrodermic, pustular or unstable psoriasis; face, flexures, genitals

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe (not mutagenic in humans).

## Viva points
- Short-contact therapy reduces staining and irritation
- Ingram regimen
- Salicylic acid stabilises dithranol (prevents oxidation)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.28 (Anthralin — dithranol, dithranol pomade); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
